flavor.1: While it is young, it uses the nutrients that are stored in the seed on its back in order to grow.
flavor.2: Exposure to sunlight adds to its strength. Sunlight also makes the bud on its back grow larger.
flavor.3: A bewitching aroma wafts from its flower. The fragrance becalms those engaged in a battle.
flavor.4: From the time it is born, a flame burns at the tip of its tail. Its life would end if the flame were to go out.
flavor.5: If it becomes agitated during battle, it spouts intense flames, incinerating its surroundings.
flavor.6: Its wings can carry this Pokémon close to an altitude of 4,600 feet. It blows out fire at very high temperatures.
flavor.7: When it feels threatened, it draws its limbs inside its shell and sprays water from its mouth.
flavor.8: It cleverly controls its furry ears and tail to maintain its balance while swimming.
flavor.9: The rocket cannons on its shell fire jets of water capable of punching holes through thick steel.
flavor.10: Its short feet are tipped with suction pads that enable it to tirelessly climb slopes and walls.
flavor.11: Even though it is encased in a sturdy shell, the body inside is tender. It can’t withstand a harsh attack.
flavor.12: It collects honey every day. It rubs honey onto the hairs on its legs to carry it back to its nest.
flavor.13: Beware of the sharp stinger on its head. It hides in grass and bushes where it eats leaves.
flavor.14: Able to move only slightly. When endangered, it may stick out its stinger and poison its enemy.
flavor.15: It has three poisonous stingers on its forelegs and its tail. They are used to jab its enemy repeatedly.
flavor.16: Very docile. If attacked, it will often kick up sand to protect itself rather than fight back.
flavor.17: This Pokémon is full of vitality. It constantly flies around its large territory in search of prey.
flavor.18: This Pokémon flies at Mach 2 speed, seeking prey. Its large talons are feared as wicked weapons.
flavor.19: Will chew on anything with its fangs. If you see one, you can be certain that 40 more live in the area.
flavor.20: Its hind feet are webbed. They act as flippers, so it can swim in rivers and hunt for prey.
flavor.21: Inept at flying high. However, it can fly around very fast to protect its territory.
flavor.22: A Pokémon that dates back many years. If it senses danger, it flies high and away, instantly.
flavor.23: The older it gets, the longer it grows. At night, it wraps its long body around tree branches to rest.
flavor.24: The frightening patterns on its belly have been studied. Six variations have been confirmed.
flavor.25: Possesses cheek sacs in which it stores electricity. This clever forest-dweller roasts tough berries with an electric shock before consuming them.
flavor.26: It can discharge bursts of electricity exceeding 100,000 volts— a single strike with that amount of power would incapacitate one of the Copperajah of my homeland.
flavor.27: It burrows into the ground to create its nest. If hard stones impede its tunneling, it uses its sharp claws to shatter them and then carries on digging.
flavor.28: It climbs trees by hooking on with its sharp claws. Sandslash shares the berries it gathers, dropping them down to Sandshrew waiting below the tree.
flavor.29: It uses its hard incisor teeth to crush and eat berries. The tip of a female Nidoran’s horn is a bit more rounded than the tip of a male’s horn.
flavor.30: If the group is threatened, these Pokémon will band together to assault enemies with a chorus of ultrasonic waves.
flavor.31: It pacifies offspring by placing them in the gaps between the spines on its back. The spines will never secrete poison while young are present.
flavor.32: Small but brave, this Pokémon will hold its ground and even risk its life in battle to protect the female it’s friendly with.
flavor.33: It’s nervous and quick to act aggressively. The potency of its poison increases along with the level of adrenaline present in its body.
flavor.34: Nidoking prides itself on its strength. It’s forceful and spirited in battle, making use of its thick tail and diamond-crushing horn.
flavor.35: It can be found in quiet mountain areas on a full moon's night. Its dancing and its tiny, faintly glowing wings confer upon it a lovely fairylike quality.
flavor.36: Legend says that on clear, quiet nights, it listens for the voices of its kin living on the moon. I, too, often think of my homeland, so far away.
flavor.37: In its belly burns a fire, which Vulpix spits out in the form of fireballs. When young, this Pokémon has but one white tail. As the Pokémon matures, this single tail splits into six.
flavor.38: The coat of gleaming golden fur is quite magnificent. This species is said to store sacred power in its nine long tails and to live for a millennium.
flavor.39: By freely changing the wavelength of its voice, Jigglypuff sings a mysterious melody sure to make any listener sleepy.
flavor.40: It’s proud of its fur, which is fine and delicate. In particular, the curl on its forehead has a texture that’s perfectly heavenly.
flavor.41: Makes its home in gloomy caves. Atrophied eyes have left this Pokémon blind, so it scans its surroundings via sound waves that it emits from its mouth as it flies.
flavor.42: It sinks its sharp fangs into other creatures and slurps up their blood. A closer look at the fangs reveals that they are hollow and akin to straws.
flavor.43: During the day, it stays in the cold underground to avoid the sun. It grows by bathing in moonlight.
flavor.44: What appears to be drool is actually sweet honey. It is very sticky and clings stubbornly if touched.
flavor.45: The larger its petals, the more toxic pollen it contains. Its big head is heavy and hard to hold up.
flavor.46: Sometimes seen at the foot of trees in humid forests. The mushrooms on its back—called tochukaso—are not present on infant specimens and instead emerge as Paras matures.
flavor.47: Mushroom-lacking specimens of this Pokémon lie unmoving in the forest, lending credence to the hypothesis that the large mushroom is in control of Parasect's actions.
flavor.48: Its large eyes act as radar. In a bright place, you can see that they are clusters of many tiny eyes.
flavor.49: The powdery scales on its wings are hard to remove from skin. They also contain poison that leaks out on contact.
flavor.50: It burrows through the ground at a shallow depth. It leaves raised earth in its wake, making it easy to spot.
flavor.51: These Diglett triplets dig over 60 miles below sea level. No one knows what it’s like underground.
flavor.52: It washes its face regularly to keep the coin on its forehead spotless. It doesn’t get along with Galarian Meowth.
flavor.53: Its elegant and refined behavior clashes with that of the barbaric Perrserker. The relationship between the two is one of mutual disdain.
flavor.54: Suffers perpetual headaches. If the agony grows too great, Psyduck's latent power erupts, contrary to Psyduck's intent. Ergo, I am exploring ways to ease the pain.
flavor.55: Its body is strong, and it has webbing on its hands and feet. Golduck can swim easily through rough seas, clawing its way through the high waves.
flavor.56: An agile Pokémon that lives in trees. It angers easily and will not hesitate to attack anything.
flavor.57: It stops being angry only when nobody else is around. To view this moment is very difficult.
flavor.58: They patrol their territory in pairs. I believe the igneous rock components in the fur of this species are the result of volcanic activity in its habitat.
flavor.59: Snaps at its foes with fangs cloaked in blazing flame. Despite its bulk, it deftly feints every which way, leading opponents on a deceptively merry chase as it all but dances around them.
flavor.60: In rivers with fast-flowing water, this Pokémon will cling to a rock by using its thick lips, which act like a suction cup.
flavor.61: This Pokémon’s sweat is a slimy mucus. When captured, Poliwhirl can slither from its enemies’ grasp and escape.
flavor.62: Poliwrath is skilled at both swimming and martial arts. It uses its well-trained arms to dish out powerful punches.
flavor.63: Spends 18 hours of the day sleeping. Even while asleep, Abra can control its psychic powers—should danger approach, the Pokémon will simply teleport away.
flavor.64: There are rumors that a child with mystical powers became a Kadabra; however, this remains unverified. I suspect that the spoon Kadabra holds enhances its brain waves.
flavor.65: The longer Alakazam lives, the larger and heavier its head becomes. Our tests have shown that the strength of its psychic powers correlates positively to the weight of its head.
flavor.66: Though as small as a child, it has strength enough to easily throw a well-built adult. Striving to become ever stronger, Machop trains by carrying a Graveler on its shoulders.
flavor.67: A sturdy creature boasting a robust physique and boundless stamina. Loves training above all else and voluntarily assists with tasks such as construction and clearing land.
flavor.68: In close combat, its four arms afford it offensive and defensive supremacy. In but a blink, this valiant Pokémon can overwhelm its foes with more than 1,000 blows from its fists.
flavor.69: Prefers hot and humid places. It ensnares tiny bugs with its vines and devours them.
flavor.70: When hungry, it swallows anything that moves. Its hapless prey is dissolved by strong acids.
flavor.71: Lures prey with the sweet aroma of honey. Swallowed whole, the prey is dissolved in a day, bones and all.
flavor.72: They fire beams from the glassy, magenta orbs that resemble eyes atop their heads, and they drift in shallow seas. During low tide, they can sometimes be found on beaches, desiccated.
flavor.73: It has 80 tentacles, each with a venomous tip. These tentacles are also extendible, lengthening when Tentacruel attempts to catch prey. Use caution.
flavor.74: Makes its home in mountainous regions, using its arms to climb along harsh mountain roads. Can be troublesome—carelessly kicking one will cause it to fly into a rage and chase after you.
flavor.75: Dwells in holes dug into sheer walls of stone. It enjoys rolling down slopes as though it were a boulder during a rockfall, so keep an eye upward while traversing mountain roads.
flavor.76: The rocklike shell is shed each year. The cast-off shell then crumbles, reverting to a mass of soil, which can be spread across fields to promote crop growth.
flavor.77: These Pokémon live in herds out in the grassland. Newborn foals lack their fiery manes, which will develop about an hour after birth.
flavor.78: Fiery mane aglow, Rapidash darts like an arrow across the land. This prodigiously swift creature can traverse the vast region of Hisui in a day and a half.
flavor.79: When this Pokémon’s tail is soaked in water, sweetness seeps from it. Slowpoke uses this trait to lure in and fish up other Pokémon.
flavor.80: Being bitten by a Shellder shocked this Pokémon into standing on two legs. If the Shellder lets go, it seems Slowbro will turn back into a Slowpoke.
flavor.81: A bizarre Pokémon with but a single eye embedded in an iron sphere. I suspect this creature levitates due to the magnetism it emits from its arms, which resemble horseshoe-shaped magnets.
flavor.82: Three Magnemite gathered to evolve into this Pokémon. The source of much vexation on my part, as its powerful magnetism destroys my research equipment.
flavor.83: They use a plant stalk as a weapon, but not all of them use it in the same way. Several distinct styles of stalk fighting have been observed.
flavor.84: Its short wings make flying difficult. Instead, this Pokémon runs at high speed on developed legs.
flavor.85: One of Doduo’s two heads splits to form a unique species. It runs close to 40 mph in prairies.
flavor.86: Loves freezing-cold conditions. Relishes swimming in a frigid climate of around 14 degrees Fahrenheit.
flavor.87: Its entire body is a snowy white. Unharmed by even intense cold, it swims powerfully in icy waters.
flavor.88: Made of congealed sludge. It smells too putrid to touch. Even weeds won’t grow in its path.
flavor.89: Smells so awful, it can cause fainting. Through degeneration of its nose, it lost its sense of smell.
flavor.90: Its hard shell repels any kind of attack. It is vulnerable only when its shell is open.
flavor.91: Once it slams its shell shut, it is impossible to open, even by those with superior strength.
flavor.92: Gaseous and completely impalpable. Also highly dangerous— inhaling part of its poisonous body will cause one to faint instantly.
flavor.93: This frightful, malevolent spirit can glide through walls, appearing wherever it likes. According to rumor, victims of a Haunter's lick will wither to death day by day.
flavor.94: Possesses potential victims' shadows in an effort to steal away the victims' lives. If your shadow begins to laugh, you must take hold of a protective charm posthaste!
flavor.95: This chain of immense stones resembles a giant serpent. Tremors shake the earth above as it burrows deep beneath the ground, feeding on boulders as it goes.
flavor.96: If you sleep by it all the time, it will sometimes show you dreams it had eaten in the past.
flavor.97: Avoid eye contact if you come across one. It will try to put you to sleep by using its pendulum.
flavor.98: If it senses danger approaching, it cloaks itself with bubbles from its mouth so it will look bigger.
flavor.99: Its oversized claw is very powerful, but when it’s not in battle, the claw just gets in the way.
flavor.100: An enigmatic Pokémon that happens to bear a resemblance to a Poké Ball. When excited, it discharges the electric current it has stored in its belly, then lets out a great, uproarious laugh.
flavor.101: The tissue on the surface of its body is curiously similar in composition to an Apricorn. When irritated, this Pokémon lets loose an electric current equal to 20 lightning bolts.
flavor.102: These Pokémon get nervous when they’re not in a group of six. The minute even one member of the group goes missing, Exeggcute become cowardly.
flavor.103: When they work together, Exeggutor’s three heads can put out powerful psychic energy. Cloudy days make this Pokémon sluggish.
flavor.104: This Pokémon wears the skull of its deceased mother. Sometimes Cubone’s dreams make it cry, but each tear Cubone sheds makes it stronger.
flavor.105: When this Pokémon evolved, the skull of its mother fused to it. Marowak’s temperament also turned vicious at the same time.
flavor.106: The legs freely contract and stretch. The stretchy legs allow it to hit a distant foe with a rising kick.
flavor.107: Its punches slice the air. However, it seems to need a short break after fighting for three minutes.
flavor.108: Wields its long tongue deftly, as though it were an arm. The Pokémon's viscous saliva, once it has been collected and boiled down, yields a strong and highly useful adhesive.
flavor.109: It adores polluted air. Some claim that Koffing used to be more plentiful in the Galar region than they are now.
flavor.110: It can’t suck in air quite as well as a Galarian Weezing, but the toxins it creates are more potent than those of its counterpart.
flavor.111: Ludicrously strong—when it butts heads with a mountain, it is the mountain that shatters. But its short legs struggle with turns, and it is incapable of stopping unless it collides with something.
flavor.112: Rapidly rotates its horn to bore through bedrock. It swaggers around volcanic regions, protected from the lava's heat by its tough, armorlike hide.
flavor.113: This purehearted Pokémon shares its eggs with the injured.
flavor.114: It is cloaked entirely in blue vines, preventing any glimpse of its true identity. The vines impart a refreshing sensation when chewed—they're useful as a spice.
flavor.115: There are records of a lost human child being raised by a childless Kangaskhan.
flavor.116: They swim with dance-like motions and cause whirlpools to form. Horsea compete to see which of them can generate the biggest whirlpool.
flavor.117: Seadra’s mouth is slender, but its suction power is strong. In an instant, Seadra can suck in food that’s larger than the opening of its mouth.
flavor.118: Its dorsal and pectoral fins are strongly developed like muscles. It can swim at a speed of five knots.
flavor.119: Using its horn, it bores holes in riverbed boulders, making nests to prevent its eggs from washing away.
flavor.120: Fish Pokémon nibble at it, but Staryu isn’t bothered. Its body regenerates quickly, even if part of it is completely torn off.
flavor.121: Starmie swims by spinning its body at high speed. As this Pokémon cruises through the ocean, it absorbs tiny plankton.
flavor.122: The behavior of this clown-like Pokémon reminds one of pantomime. It creates invisible walls using a force emitted from its fingertips.
flavor.123: The large, wickedly sharp scythes on its forearms are truly fearsome weapons. Prey's attempts to flee are unfailingly thwarted by this Pokémon's nimble motions.
flavor.124: The Jynx of Galar often have beautiful and delicate voices. Some of these Pokémon have even gathered a fan base.
flavor.125: Feeds on electrical energy. During sudden showers beneath looming thunderclouds, one can observe Electabuzz scaling tall trees, where the Pokémon will then wait for lightning to strike.
flavor.126: Legend has it that this Pokémon was born from the crater of a volcano. When wounded, it bathes in lava to heal its body, much as one would soak in a hot spring.
flavor.127: This Pokémon clamps its pincers down on its prey and then either splits the prey in half or flings it away.
flavor.128: The Tauros of the Galar region are volatile in nature, and they won’t allow people to ride on their backs.
flavor.129: A feeble, pitiful imbecile of a Pokémon that is nonetheless very hardy. Unperturbed by turbid water, it can be found living in all sorts of places.
flavor.130: I suspect this Pokémon to be the true identity of a dragon written of in ancient texts, which claimed that it razed an entire village with white-hot beams from its maw.
flavor.131: Crossing icy seas is no issue for this cold-resistant Pokémon. Its smooth skin is a little cool to the touch.
flavor.132: When it encounters another Ditto, it will move faster than normal to duplicate that opponent exactly.
flavor.133: Harbors the potential to evolve into manifold forms. Within Eevee lies the key to the mysteries of Pokémon evolution—I'm certain of it.
flavor.134: Tests show that its cells closely resemble water molecules, which perhaps explains its ability to conceal its form while submerged. I believe the origins of mermaid folklore lie with this Pokémon.
flavor.135: Bristles its fur into sharp, needlelike points when enraged. One can hear electricity crackle in its breath when it exhales.
flavor.136: Flames burn within a saclike organ inside this Pokémon. When Flareon inhales, these flames grow in intensity, reaching a mighty 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit.
flavor.137: It has no discernible heartbeat and does not seem to draw breath, and yet it appears to function without issue. I cannot even begin to explain this utterly bizarre anomaly.
flavor.138: This Pokémon is a member of an ancient, extinct species. Omanyte paddles through water with its 10 tentacles, looking like it’s just drifting along.
flavor.139: Omastar’s sharp fangs could crush rock, but the Pokémon can attack only the prey that come within reach of its tentacles.
flavor.140: While some say this species has gone extinct, Kabuto sightings are apparently fairly common in some places.
flavor.141: The cause behind the extinction of this species is unknown. Kabutops were aggressive Pokémon that inhabited warm seas.
flavor.142: Aerodactyl’s sawlike fangs can shred skin to tatters—even the skin of Steel-type Pokémon.
flavor.143: This glutton appears in villages without warning and devours the entirety of their rice granaries—such occurrences have long been counted among the gravest of disasters.
flavor.144: This Pokémon can control ice at will. Articuno is said to live in snowy mountains riddled with permafrost.
flavor.145: Zapdos is a legendary bird Pokémon. It’s said that when Zapdos rubs its feathers together, lightning will fall immediately after.
flavor.146: There are stories of this Pokémon using its radiant, flame-cloaked wings to light up paths for those lost in the mountains.
flavor.147: This Pokémon was long considered to be no more than a myth. The small lump on a Dratini’s forehead is actually a horn that’s still coming in.
flavor.148: This Pokémon gathers power in the orbs on its tail and controls the weather. When enshrouded by an aura, Dragonair has a mystical appearance.
flavor.149: This Pokémon is known as the Sea Incarnate. Figureheads that resemble Dragonite decorate the bows of many ships.
flavor.150: Its DNA is almost the same as Mew’s. However, its size and disposition are vastly different.
flavor.151: When viewed through a microscope, this Pokémon’s short, fine, delicate hair can be seen.

1.name: Stench
1.desc: By releasing a stench when attacking, the Pokémon may cause the target to flinch.

2.name: Drizzle
2.desc: The Pokémon makes it rain when it enters a battle.

3.name: Speed Boost
3.desc: The Pokémon's Speed stat is boosted every turn.

4.name: Battle Armor
4.desc: Hard armor protects the Pokémon from critical hits.

5.name: Sturdy
5.desc: The Pokémon cannot be knocked out by a single hit as long as its HP is full. One-hit KO moves will also fail to knock it out.

6.name: Damp
6.desc: The Pokémon dampens its surroundings, preventing all Pokémon from using explosive moves such as Self-Destruct.

7.name: Limber
7.desc: The Pokémon's limber body prevents it from being paralyzed.

8.name: Sand Veil
8.desc: Boosts the Pokémon's evasiveness in a sandstorm.

9.name: Static
9.desc: The Pokémon is charged with static electricity and may paralyze attackers that make direct contact with it.

10.name: Volt Absorb
10.desc: If hit by an Electric-type move, the Pokémon has its HP restored instead of taking damage.

11.name: Water Absorb
11.desc: If hit by a Water-type move, the Pokémon has its HP restored instead of taking damage.

12.name: Oblivious
12.desc: The Pokémon is oblivious, keeping it from being infatuated, falling for taunts, or being affected by Intimidate.

14.name: Compound Eyes
14.desc: The Pokémon's compound eyes boost its accuracy.

15.name: Insomnia
15.desc: The Pokémon's insomnia prevents it from falling asleep.

16.name: Color Change
16.desc: The Pokémon’s type becomes the type of the move used on it.

17.name: Immunity
17.desc: The Pokémon's immune system prevents it from being poisoned.

18.name: Flash Fire
18.desc: If hit by a Fire-type move, the Pokémon absorbs the flames and uses them to power up its own Fire-type moves.

19.name: Shield Dust
19.desc: Protective dust shields the Pokémon from the additional effects of moves.

20.name: Own Tempo
20.desc: The Pokémon sticks to its own tempo, preventing it from becoming confused or being affected by Intimidate.

21.name: Suction Cups
21.desc: The Pokémon uses suction cups to stay in one spot. This protects it from moves and items that would force it to switch out.

22.name: Intimidate
22.desc: When the Pokémon enters a battle, it intimidates opposing Pokémon and makes them cower, lowering their Attack stats.

23.name: Shadow Tag
23.desc: The Pokémon steps on the opposing Pokémon's shadows to prevent them from fleeing or switching out.

24.name: Rough Skin
24.desc: The Pokémon's rough skin damages attackers that make direct contact with it.

25.name: Wonder Guard
25.desc: Its mysterious power only lets supereffective moves hit the Pokémon.

26.name: Levitate
26.desc: By floating in the air, the Pokémon receives full immunity to all Ground-type moves.

27.name: Effect Spore
27.desc: Contact with the Pokémon may inflict poison, sleep, or paralysis on the attacker.

28.name: Synchronize
28.desc: If the Pokémon is burned, paralyzed, or poisoned by another Pokémon, that Pokémon will be inflicted with the same status condition.

29.name: Clear Body
29.desc: Prevents other Pokémon's moves or Abilities from lowering the Pokémon's stats.

30.name: Natural Cure
30.desc: The Pokémon's status conditions are cured when it switches out.

31.name: Lightning Rod
31.desc: The Pokémon draws in all Electric-type moves. Instead of taking damage from them, its Sp. Atk stat is boosted.

32.name: Serene Grace
32.desc: Raises the likelihood of additional effects occurring when the Pokémon uses its moves.

33.name: Swift Swim
33.desc: Boosts the Pokémon's Speed stat in rain.

34.name: Chlorophyll
34.desc: Boosts the Pokémon's Speed stat in harsh sunlight.

35.name: Illuminate
35.desc: By illuminating its surroundings, the Pokémon prevents its accuracy from being lowered.

36.name: Trace
36.desc: When it enters a battle, the Pokémon copies an opposing Pokémon's Ability.

38.name: Poison Point
38.desc: Contact with the Pokémon may poison the attacker.

39.name: Inner Focus
39.desc: The Pokémon's intense focus prevents it from flinching or being affected by Intimidate.

40.name: Magma Armor
40.desc: The Pokémon’s hot magma coating prevents it from being frozen.

41.name: Water Veil
41.desc: The Pokémon's water veil prevents it from being burned.

42.name: Magnet Pull
42.desc: Prevents Steel-type Pokémon from fleeing by pulling them in with magnetism.

43.name: Soundproof
43.desc: Soundproofing gives the Pokémon full immunity to all sound-based moves.

44.name: Rain Dish
44.desc: The Pokémon gradually regains HP in rain.

45.name: Sand Stream
45.desc: The Pokémon summons a sandstorm when it enters a battle.

46.name: Pressure
46.desc: Puts other Pokémon under pressure, causing them to expend more PP to use their moves.

47.name: Thick Fat
47.desc: The Pokémon is protected by a layer of thick fat, which halves the damage taken from Fire- and Ice-type moves.

48.name: Early Bird
48.desc: The Pokémon awakens from sleep twice as fast as other Pokémon.

49.name: Flame Body
49.desc: Contact with the Pokémon may burn the attacker.

50.name: Run Away
50.desc: Enables a sure getaway from wild Pokémon.

51.name: Keen Eye
51.desc: The Pokémon's keen eyes prevent its accuracy from being lowered.

52.name: Hyper Cutter
52.desc: The Pokémon's prized, mighty pincers prevent other Pokémon from lowering its Attack stat.

53.name: Pickup
53.desc: The Pokémon may pick up an item another Pokémon used during a battle. It may pick up items outside of battle, too.

54.name: Truant
54.desc: Each time the Pokémon uses a move, it spends the next turn loafing around.

55.name: Hustle
55.desc: Boosts the Pokémon's Attack stat but lowers its accuracy.

56.name: Cute Charm
56.desc: The Pokémon may infatuate attackers that make direct contact with it.

57.name: Plus
57.desc: Boosts the Sp. Atk stat of the Pokémon if an ally with the Plus or Minus Ability is also in battle.

58.name: Minus
58.desc: Boosts the Sp. Atk stat of the Pokémon if an ally with the Plus or Minus Ability is also in battle.

59.name: Forecast
59.desc: The Pokémon transforms with the weather to change its type to Water, Fire, or Ice.

60.name: Sticky Hold
60.desc: The Pokémon's held items cling to its sticky body and cannot be removed by other Pokémon.

61.name: Shed Skin
61.desc: The Pokémon may cure its own status conditions by shedding its skin.

62.name: Guts
62.desc: It's so gutsy that having a status condition boosts the Pokémon's Attack stat.

63.name: Marvel Scale
63.desc: The Pokémon's marvelous scales boost its Defense stat if it has a status condition.

64.name: Liquid Ooze
64.desc: The strong stench of the Pokémon's oozed liquid damages attackers that use HP-draining moves.

65.name: Overgrow
65.desc: Powers up Grass-type moves when the Pokémon's HP is low.

66.name: Blaze
66.desc: Powers up Fire-type moves when the Pokémon's HP is low.

67.name: Torrent
67.desc: Powers up Water-type moves when the Pokémon's HP is low.

68.name: Swarm
68.desc: Powers up Bug-type moves when the Pokémon's HP is low.

69.name: Rock Head
69.desc: Protects the Pokémon from recoil damage.

70.name: Drought
70.desc: Turns the sunlight harsh when the Pokémon enters a battle.

71.name: Arena Trap
71.desc: Prevents opposing Pokémon from fleeing from battle.

72.name: Vital Spirit
72.desc: The Pokémon is full of vitality, and that prevents it from falling asleep.

73.name: White Smoke
73.desc: The Pokémon is protected by its white smoke, which prevents other Pokémon from lowering its stats.

74.name: Pure Power
74.desc: Using its pure power, the Pokémon doubles its Attack stat.

75.name: Shell Armor
75.desc: A hard shell protects the Pokémon from critical hits.

77.name: Tangled Feet
77.desc: Boosts the Pokémon's evasiveness if it is confused.

78.name: Motor Drive
78.desc: The Pokémon takes no damage when hit by Electric-type moves. Instead, its Speed stat is boosted.

79.name: Rivalry
79.desc: The Pokémon's competitive spirit makes it deal more damage to Pokémon of the same gender, but less damage to Pokémon of the opposite gender.

80.name: Steadfast
80.desc: The Pokémon's determination boosts its Speed stat every time it flinches.

81.name: Snow Cloak
81.desc: Boosts the Pokémon's evasiveness in snow.

82.name: Gluttony
82.desc: If the Pokémon is holding a Berry to be eaten when its HP is low, it will instead eat the Berry when its HP drops to half or less.

83.name: Anger Point
83.desc: The Pokémon is angered when it takes a critical hit, and that maxes its Attack stat.

84.name: Unburden
84.desc: Boosts the Speed stat if the Pokémon's held item is used or lost.

85.name: Heatproof
85.desc: The Pokémon's heatproof body halves the damage taken from Fire-type moves.

86.name: Simple
86.desc: Doubles the effects of the Pokémon's stat changes.

87.name: Dry Skin
87.desc: Restores the Pokémon's HP in rain or when it is hit by Water-type moves. Reduces HP in harsh sunlight, and increases the damage received from Fire-type moves.

88.name: Download
88.desc: The Pokémon compares an opposing Pokémon's Defense and Sp. Def stats before raising its own Attack or Sp. Atk stat—whichever will be more effective.

90.name: Poison Heal
90.desc: If poisoned, the Pokémon has its HP restored instead of taking damage.

91.name: Adaptability
91.desc: Powers up moves of the same type as the Pokémon.

92.name: Skill Link
92.desc: Maximizes the number of times multistrike moves hit.

115.desc: The Pokémon gradually regains HP in snow.

116.desc: Reduces the power of supereffective attacks that hit the Pokémon.

119.desc: When it enters a battle, the Pokémon can check an opposing Pokémon's held item.

121.desc: Changes the Pokémon's type to match the plate it holds.

130.desc: May disable a move that has dealt damage to the Pokémon.

131.desc: Sometimes cures the status conditions of the Pokémon's allies.

133.desc: The Pokémon's Defense stat is lowered when it takes damage from physical moves, but its Speed stat is sharply boosted.

139.name: Harvest
139.desc: May create another Berry after one is used.

140.name: Telepathy
140.desc: The Pokémon anticipates and dodges the attacks of its allies.

141.name: Moody
141.desc: Every turn, one of the Pokémon's stats will be boosted sharply but another stat will be lowered.

142.name: Overcoat
142.desc: The Pokémon takes no damage from sandstorms. It is also protected from the effects of powders and spores.

143.name: Poison Touch
143.desc: May poison a target when the Pokémon makes contact.

144.name: Regenerator
144.desc: The Pokémon has a little of its HP restored when withdrawn from battle.

145.name: Big Pecks
145.desc: Prevents the Pokémon from having its Defense stat lowered.

146.name: Sand Rush
146.desc: Boosts the Pokémon's Speed stat in a sandstorm.

147.name: Wonder Skin
147.desc: Makes status moves more likely to miss the Pokémon.

148.desc: Boosts the power of the Pokémon's move if it is the last to act that turn.

149.desc: The Pokémon fools opponents by entering battle disguised as the last Pokémon in its Trainer's party.

150.name: Imposter
150.desc: The Pokémon transforms itself into the Pokémon it's facing.

151.name: Infiltrator
151.desc: The Pokémon's moves are unaffected by the target's barriers, substitutes, and the like.

152.desc: Contact with the Pokémon changes the attacker’s Ability to Mummy.

153.desc: When the Pokémon knocks out a target, it shows moxie, which boosts its Attack stat.

154.desc: When the Pokémon is hit by a Dark-type attack, its Attack stat is boosted by its sense of justice.

155.desc: The Pokémon gets scared when hit by a Dark-, Ghost-, or Bug-type attack or if intimidated, which boosts its Speed stat.

156.desc: The Pokémon reflects status moves instead of getting hit by them.

157.desc: The Pokémon takes no damage when hit by Grass-type moves. Instead, its Attack stat is boosted.

158.desc: Gives priority to the Pokémon's status moves.

159.name: Sand Force
159.desc: Boosts the power of Rock-, Ground-, and Steel-type moves in a sandstorm.

160.name: Iron Barbs
160.desc: Inflicts damage on the attacker upon contact with iron barbs.

161.name: Zen Mode
161.desc: Changes the Pokémon’s shape when HP is half or less.

162.name: Victory Star
162.desc: Boosts the accuracy of its allies and itself.

163.desc: The Pokémon's moves are unimpeded by the Ability of the target.

164.name: Teravolt
164.desc: The Pokémon's moves are unimpeded by the Ability of the target.

165.desc: Protects the Pokémon and its allies from effects that prevent the use of moves.

166.name: Flower Veil
166.desc: Ally Grass-type Pokémon are protected from status conditions and the lowering of their stats.

167.desc: The Pokémon's HP is restored when it eats any Berry, in addition to the Berry's usual effect.

168.desc: Changes the Pokémon's type to the type of the move it's about to use. This works only once each time the Pokémon enters battle.

169.name: Fur Coat
169.desc: Halves the damage from physical moves.

170.name: Magician
170.desc: The Pokémon steals the held item from any target it hits with a move.

171.name: Bulletproof
171.desc: Protects the Pokémon from ball and bomb moves.

172.name: Competitive
172.desc: Boosts the Pokémon's Sp. Atk stat sharply when its stats are lowered by an opposing Pokémon.

173.name: Strong Jaw
173.desc: The Pokémon's strong jaw boosts the power of its biting moves.

174.name: Refrigerate
174.desc: Normal-type moves become Ice-type moves. The power of those moves is boosted a little.

175.name: Sweet Veil
175.desc: Prevents the Pokémon and its allies from falling asleep.

176.name: Stance Change
176.desc: The Pokémon changes its form to Blade Forme when it uses an attack move and changes to Shield Forme when it uses King’s Shield.

177.name: Gale Wings
177.desc: Gives priority to the Pokémon's Flying-type moves while its HP is full.

179.name: Grass Pelt
179.desc: Boosts the Pokémon's Defense stat on Grassy Terrain.

180.name: Symbiosis
180.desc: The Pokémon passes its held item to an ally that has used up an item.

181.name: Tough Claws
181.desc: Powers up moves that make direct contact.

182.name: Pixilate
182.desc: Normal-type moves become Fairy-type moves. The power of those moves is boosted a little.

183.name: Gooey
183.desc: Contact with the Pokémon lowers the attacker's Speed stat.

184.name: Aerilate
184.desc: Normal-type moves become Flying-type moves. The power of those moves is boosted a little.

186.name: Dark Aura
186.desc: Powers up each Pokémon’s Dark-type moves.

187.name: Fairy Aura
187.desc: Powers up each Pokémon’s Fairy-type moves.

188.name: Aura Break
188.desc: The effects of “Aura” Abilities are reversed to lower the power of affected moves.

189.name: Primordial Sea
189.desc: The Pokémon changes the weather to nullify Fire-type attacks.

190.name: Desolate Land
190.desc: The Pokémon changes the weather to nullify Water-type attacks.

191.name: Delta Stream
191.desc: The Pokémon changes the weather to eliminate all of the Flying type’s weaknesses.

192.name: Stamina
192.desc: Boosts the Defense stat when the Pokémon is hit by an attack.

193.name: Wimp Out
193.desc: The Pokémon cowardly switches out when its HP becomes half or less.

194.name: Emergency Exit
194.desc: The Pokémon, sensing danger, switches out when its HP becomes half or less.

195.name: Water Compaction
195.desc: Boosts the Defense stat sharply when the Pokémon is hit by a Water-type move.

196.name: Merciless
196.desc: The Pokémon's attacks become critical hits if the target is poisoned.

197.name: Shields Down
197.desc: When its HP drops to half or less, the Pokémon's shell breaks and it becomes aggressive.

198.name: Stakeout
198.desc: Doubles the damage dealt to a target that has just switched into battle.

199.name: Water Bubble
199.desc: Lowers the power of Fire-type moves that hit the Pokémon and prevents it from being burned.

201.name: Berserk
201.desc: Boosts the Pokémon's Sp. Atk stat when it takes a hit that causes its HP to drop to half or less.

202.name: Slush Rush
202.desc: Boosts the Pokémon's Speed stat in snow.

203.name: Long Reach
203.desc: The Pokémon uses its moves without making contact with the target.

205.name: Triage
205.desc: Gives priority to the Pokémon's healing moves.

206.name: Galvanize
206.desc: Normal-type moves become Electric-type moves. The power of those moves is boosted a little.

207.name: Surge Surfer
207.desc: Doubles the Pokémon's Speed stat on Electric Terrain.

208.name: Schooling
208.desc: When it has a lot of HP, the Pokémon forms a powerful school. It stops schooling when its HP is low.

209.name: Disguise
209.desc: Once per battle, the shroud that covers the Pokémon can protect it from an attack.

210.name: Battle Bond
210.desc: When the Pokémon knocks out a target, its bond with its Trainer is strengthened, and its Attack, Sp. Atk, and Speed stats are boosted.

211.name: Power Construct
211.desc: Other Cells gather to aid when its HP becomes half or less. Then the Pokémon changes its form to Complete Forme.

212.name: Corrosion
212.desc: The Pokémon can poison the target even if it's a Steel or Poison type.

213.name: Comatose
213.desc: The Pokémon is always drowsing and will never wake up. It can attack while in its sleeping state.

214.name: Queenly Majesty
214.desc: When the Pokémon uses Surf or Dive, it will come back with prey. When it takes damage, it will spit out the prey to attack.

215.name: Innards Out
215.desc: Damages the attacker landing the finishing hit by the amount equal to its last HP.

216.name: Dancer
216.desc: Whenever a dance move is used in battle, the Pokémon will copy the user to immediately perform that dance move itself.

217.name: Battery
217.desc: Powers up ally Pokémon's special moves.

218.name: Fluffy
218.desc: Halves the damage taken from moves that make direct contact, but doubles that of Fire-type moves.

219.name: Dazzling
219.desc: The Pokémon dazzles its opponents, making them unable to use priority moves against the Pokémon or its allies.

220.name: Soul-Heart
220.desc: Boosts the Pokémon's Sp. Atk stat every time another Pokémon faints.

221.name: Tangling Hair
221.desc: Contact with the Pokémon lowers the attacker's Speed stat.

222.name: Receiver
222.desc: The Pokémon copies the Ability of a defeated ally.

223.name: Power of Alchemy
223.desc: The Pokémon copies the Ability of a defeated ally.

224.name: Beast Boost
224.desc: The Pokémon boosts its most proficient stat each time it knocks out a Pokémon.

225.name: RKS System
225.desc: Changes the Pokémon’s type to match the memory disc it holds.

228.desc: Turns the ground into Misty Terrain when the Pokémon enters a battle.

229.desc: Turns the ground into Grassy Terrain when the Pokémon enters a battle.

230.desc: Prevents other Pokémon’s moves or Abilities from lowering the Pokémon’s stats.

231.desc: Reduces the amount of damage the Pokémon takes while its HP is full.

232.name: Prism Armor
232.desc: Reduces the power of supereffective attacks taken.

233.desc: Powers up moves that are super effective.

235.desc: Boosts the Pokémon’s Defense stat the first time the Pokémon enters a battle.

236.desc: Changes the Pokémon's type to the type of the move it's about to use. This works only once each time the Pokémon enters battle.

237.desc: If the Pokémon is not holding an item, it will fetch the Poké Ball from the first failed throw of the battle.

238.desc: When the Pokémon is hit by an attack, it scatters cotton fluff around and lowers the Speed stat of all Pokémon except itself.

239.desc: Ignores the effects of opposing Pokémon's Abilities and moves that draw in moves.

240.name: Mirror Armor
240.desc: Bounces back only the stat-lowering effects that the Pokémon receives.

241.desc: When the Pokémon uses Surf or Dive, it will come back with prey. When it takes damage, it will spit out the prey to attack.

242.name: Stalwart
242.desc: Ignores the effects of opposing Pokémon's Abilities and moves that draw in moves.

243.name: Steam Engine
243.desc: Boosts the Speed stat drastically when the Pokémon is hit by a Fire- or Water-type move.

244.desc: Boosts the power of sound-based moves. The Pokémon also takes half the damage from these kinds of moves.

245.desc: The Pokémon creates a sandstorm when it's hit by an attack.

246.name: Ice Scales
246.desc: The Pokémon is protected by ice scales, which halve the damage taken from special moves.

247.name: Ripen
247.desc: Ripens Berries and doubles their effect.

248.desc: The Pokémon's ice head can take a physical attack as a substitute, but the attack also changes the Pokémon's appearance. The ice will be restored when it snows.

249.name: Power Spot
249.desc: Just being next to the Pokémon powers up moves.

250.name: Mimicry
250.desc: Changes the Pokémon’s type depending on the terrain.

251.name: Screen Cleaner
251.desc: When the Pokémon enters a battle, the effects of Light Screen, Reflect, and Aurora Veil are nullified for both opposing and ally Pokémon.

252.name: Steely Spirit
252.desc: Powers up the Steel-type moves of the Pokémon and its allies.

253.desc: When hit by a move that makes direct contact, the Pokémon and the attacker will faint after three turns unless they switch out of battle.

254.name: Wandering Spirit
254.desc: The Pokémon exchanges Abilities with a Pokémon that hits it with a move that makes direct contact.

255.name: Gorilla Tactics
255.desc: Boosts the Pokémon’s Attack stat but only allows the use of the first selected move.

256.desc: While the Pokémon is in the battle, the effects of all other Pokémon's Abilities will be nullified or will not be triggered.

257.name: Pastel Veil
257.desc: Protects the Pokémon and its ally Pokémon from being poisoned.

259.desc: Enables the Pokémon to move first occasionally.

260.desc: If the Pokémon uses moves that make direct contact, it can attack the target even if the target protects itself.

261.desc: When the Pokémon enters a battle, it scatters medicine from its shell, which removes all stat changes from allies.

264.desc: When the Pokémon knocks out a target, it utters a chilling neigh, which boosts its Attack stat.

265.desc: When the Pokémon knocks out a target, it utters a terrifying neigh, which boosts its Sp. Atk stat.

267.name: As One
267.desc: This Ability combines the effects of both Calyrex's Unnerve Ability and Spectrier's Grim Neigh Ability.

268.name: Lingering Aroma
268.desc: Contact with the Pokémon changes the attacker's Ability to Lingering Aroma.

269.name: Seed Sower
269.desc: Turns the ground into Grassy Terrain when the Pokémon is hit by an attack.

270.name: Thermal Exchange
270.desc: Boosts the Attack stat when the Pokémon is hit by a Fire-type move. The Pokémon also cannot be burned.

271.desc: When an attack causes its HP to drop to half or less, the Pokémon gets angry. This lowers its Defense and Sp. Def stats but boosts its Attack, Sp. Atk, and Speed stats.

272.desc: The Pokémon's pure salt protects it from status conditions and halves the damage taken from Ghost-type moves.

273.desc: The Pokémon takes no damage when hit by Fire-type moves. Instead, its Defense stat is sharply boosted.

274.name: Wind Rider
274.desc: Boosts the Pokémon's Attack stat if Tailwind takes effect or if the Pokémon is hit by a wind move. The Pokémon also takes no damage from wind moves.

275.name: Guard Dog
275.desc: Boosts the Pokémon’s Attack stat if intimidated. Moves and items that would force the Pokémon to switch out also fail to work.

277.name: Wind Power
277.desc: The Pokémon becomes charged when it is hit by a wind move, boosting the power of the next Electric-type move the Pokémon uses.

278.name: Zero to Hero
278.desc: The Pokémon transforms into its Hero Form when it switches out.

279.desc: When the Pokémon enters a battle, it goes inside the mouth of an ally Dondozo if one is on the field. The Pokémon then issues commands from there.

280.name: Electromorphosis
280.desc: The Pokémon becomes charged when it takes damage, boosting the power of the next Electric-type move the Pokémon uses.

281.name: Protosynthesis
281.desc: Boosts the Pokémon's most proficient stat in harsh sunlight or if the Pokémon is holding Booster Energy.

282.name: Quark Drive
282.desc: Boosts the Pokémon's most proficient stat on Electric Terrain or if the Pokémon is holding Booster Energy.

283.desc: A body of pure, solid gold gives the Pokémon full immunity to other Pokémon's status moves.

284.name: Vessel of Ruin
284.desc: The power of the Pokémon's ruinous vessel lowers the Sp. Atk stats of all Pokémon except itself.

285.name: Sword of Ruin
285.desc: The power of the Pokémon's ruinous sword lowers the Defense stats of all Pokémon except itself.

286.name: Tablets of Ruin
286.desc: The power of the Pokémon's ruinous wooden tablets lowers the Attack stats of all Pokémon except itself.

287.name: Beads of Ruin
287.desc: The power of the Pokémon's ruinous beads lowers the Sp. Def stats of all Pokémon except itself.

288.desc: Turns the sunlight harsh when the Pokémon enters a battle. The ancient pulse thrumming through the Pokémon also boosts its Attack stat in harsh sunlight.

289.name: Hadron Engine
289.desc: Turns the ground into Electric Terrain when the Pokémon enters a battle. The futuristic engine within the Pokémon also boosts its Sp. Atk stat on Electric Terrain.

290.desc: If an opponent's stat is boosted, the Pokémon seizes the opportunity to boost the same stat for itself.

293.name: Supreme Overlord
293.desc: When the Pokémon enters a battle, its Attack and Sp. Atk stats are slightly boosted for each of the allies in its party that have already been defeated.

294.name: Costar
294.desc: When the Pokémon enters a battle, it copies an ally's stat changes.

295.name: Toxic Debris
295.desc: Scatters poison spikes at the feet of the opposing team when the Pokémon takes damage from physical moves.

296.name: Armor Tail
296.desc: The mysterious tail covering the Pokémon's head makes opponents unable to use priority moves against the Pokémon or its allies.

297.name: Earth Eater
297.desc: If hit by a Ground-type move, the Pokémon has its HP restored instead of taking damage.

298.name: Mycelium Might
298.desc: The Pokémon will always act more slowly when using status moves, but these moves will be unimpeded by the Ability of the target.

299.name: Mind’s Eye
299.desc: The Pokémon ignores changes to opponents' evasiveness, its accuracy can't be lowered, and it can hit Ghost types with Normal-type and Fighting-type moves

300.name: Supersweet Syrup
300.desc: Lowers the evasion of opposing Pokémon by 1 stage when first sent into battle

301.name: Hospitality
301.desc: When the Pokémon enters a battle, it showers its ally with hospitality, restoring a small amount of the ally's HP

302.name: Toxic Chain
302.desc: The power of the Pokémon's toxic chain may badly poison any target the Pokémon hits with a move

303.name: Embody Aspect
303.desc: The Pokémon's heart fills with memories, causing the Mask to shine and one of the Pokémon's stats to be boosted.

304.name: Tera Shift
304.desc: When the Pokémon enters a battle, it absorbs the energy around itself and transforms into its Terastal Form.

305.name: Tera Shell
305.desc: The Pokémon's shell contains the powers of each type. All damage-dealing moves that hit the Pokémon when its HP is full will not be very effective.

306.name: Teraform Zero
306.desc: When Terapagos changes into its Stellar Form, it uses its hidden powers to eliminate all effects of weather and terrain, reducing them to zero.

307.name: Poison Puppeteer
307.desc: Pokémon poisoned by Pecharunt's moves will also become confused.

308.name: Piercing Drill

309.name: Dragonize

310.name: Mega Sol
310.desc: Even when the sunlight has not turned harsh, the Pokémon can use its moves as if the weather were harsh sunlight.

311.name: Spicy Spray
311.desc: When the Pokémon takes damage from a move, it burns the attacker.

312.name: Eelevate
312.desc: The Pokémon floats off the ground, making it immune to Ground-type moves, as well as the Spikes, Toxic Spikes, and Sticky Web statuses. When the Pokémon knocks out a target with an attack, its highest stat is boosted by 1 stage.

313.name: Fire Mane
313.desc: Boosts the power of the Pokémon's Fire-type moves by 50%.

314.name: Aura Guard
314.desc: A Pokémon with Aura Guard takes half damage from moves that make contact. Moves affected by Long Reach which make contact will deal regular damage.

leftovers.name: Leftovers
leftovers.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. The holder’s HP is slowly but steadily restored throughout every battle.

life-orb.name: Life Orb
life-orb.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It boosts the power of moves but at the cost of some HP on each hit.

choice-band.name: Choice Band
choice-band.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. This curious headband boosts Attack but only allows the use of one move.

choice-specs.name: Choice Specs
choice-specs.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. These curious glasses boost Sp. Atk but only allow the use of one move.

choice-scarf.name: Choice Scarf
choice-scarf.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. This curious scarf boosts Speed but only allows the use of one move.

focus-band.name: Focus Band
focus-band.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. The holder may endure a potential KO attack, leaving it with just 1 HP.

focus-sash.name: Focus Sash
focus-sash.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. If the holder has full HP, it will endure a potential KO attack with 1 HP. The item then disappears.

quick-claw.name: Quick Claw
quick-claw.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. This light, sharp claw lets the bearer move first occasionally.

scope-lens.name: Scope Lens
scope-lens.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It’s a lens for scoping out weak points. It boosts the holder’s critical-hit ratio.

razor-claw.name: Razor Claw
razor-claw.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. This sharply hooked claw increases the holder’s critical-hit ratio.

wide-lens.name: Wide Lens
wide-lens.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It’s a magnifying lens that slightly boosts the accuracy of moves.

zoom-lens.name: Zoom Lens
zoom-lens.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. If the holder moves after its target moves, its accuracy will be boosted.

lucky-egg.name: Lucky Egg
lucky-egg.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It’s an egg filled with happiness that earns the holder extra Exp. Points in battle.

amulet-coin.name: Amulet Coin
amulet-coin.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It doubles any prize money received if the holding Pokémon joins a battle.

shell-bell.name: Shell Bell
shell-bell.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. The holder restores a little HP every time it inflicts damage on others.

big-root.name: Big Root
big-root.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It boosts the amount of HP the holder restores from HP-stealing moves.

black-sludge.name: Black Sludge
black-sludge.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It gradually restores HP to Poison-type Pokémon. It damages any other type.

rocky-helmet.name: Rocky Helmet
rocky-helmet.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. If the holder is hit, the attacker will also be damaged upon contact.

expert-belt.name: Expert Belt
expert-belt.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It’s a well-worn belt that slightly boosts the power of supereffective moves.

muscle-band.name: Muscle Band
muscle-band.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. This headband exudes strength, slightly boosting the power of physical moves.

wise-glasses.name: Wise Glasses
wise-glasses.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. This thick pair of glasses slightly boosts the power of special moves.

kings-rock.name: King’s Rock
kings-rock.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. When the holder successfully inflicts damage, the target may also flinch.

bright-powder.name: Bright Powder
bright-powder.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It casts a tricky glare that lowers the opposing Pokémon’s accuracy.

lax-incense.name: Lax Incense
lax-incense.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. The beguiling aroma of this incense may cause attacks to miss its holder.

metronome.name: Metronome
metronome.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It boosts moves used consecutively but only until a different move is used.

light-clay.name: Light Clay
light-clay.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. Protective moves like Light Screen and Reflect will be effective longer.

sitrus-berry.name: Sitrus Berry
sitrus-berry.desc: A Berry to be consumed by Pokémon. If a Pokémon holds one, it can restore its own HP by a small amount during battle.

oran-berry.name: Oran Berry
oran-berry.desc: A Berry to be consumed by Pokémon. If a Pokémon holds one, it can restore its own HP by 10 points during battle.

lum-berry.name: Lum Berry
lum-berry.desc: A Berry to be consumed by Pokémon. If a Pokémon holds one, it can recover from any status condition during battle.

charcoal.name: Charcoal
charcoal.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It’s a combustible fuel that boosts the power of Fire-type moves.

mystic-water.name: Mystic Water
mystic-water.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. This teardrop-shaped gem boosts the power of Water-type moves.

miracle-seed.name: Miracle Seed
miracle-seed.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It’s a seed imbued with life-force that boosts the power of Grass-type moves.

magnet.name: Magnet
magnet.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It’s a powerful magnet that boosts the power of Electric-type moves.

never-melt-ice.name: Never-Melt Ice
never-melt-ice.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It’s a heat- repelling piece of ice that boosts the power of Ice-type moves.

black-belt.name: Black Belt
black-belt.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. This belt helps the wearer to focus and boosts the power of Fighting-type moves.

poison-barb.name: Poison Barb
poison-barb.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. This small, poisonous barb boosts the power of Poison-type moves.

soft-sand.name: Soft Sand
soft-sand.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It’s a loose, silky sand that boosts the power of Ground-type moves.

sharp-beak.name: Sharp Beak
sharp-beak.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It’s a long, sharp beak that boosts the power of Flying-type moves.

twisted-spoon.name: Twisted Spoon
twisted-spoon.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. This spoon is imbued with telekinetic power and boosts Psychic-type moves.

silver-powder.name: Silver Powder
silver-powder.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It’s a shiny silver powder that will boost the power of Bug-type moves.

hard-stone.name: Hard Stone
hard-stone.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It’s a durable stone that boosts the power of Rock-type moves.

spell-tag.name: Spell Tag
spell-tag.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It’s a sinister, eerie tag that boosts the power of Ghost-type moves.

dragon-fang.name: Dragon Fang
dragon-fang.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. This hard and sharp fang boosts the power of Dragon-type moves.

black-glasses.name: Black Glasses
black-glasses.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It’s a pair of shady-looking glasses that boost the power of Dark-type moves.

metal-coat.name: Metal Coat
metal-coat.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It’s a special metallic film that can boost the power of Steel-type moves.

silk-scarf.name: Silk Scarf
silk-scarf.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It’s a sumptuous scarf that boosts the power of Normal-type moves.

assault-vest.name: Assault Vest
assault-vest.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. This offensive vest raises Sp. Def but prevents the use of status moves.

eviolite.name: Eviolite
eviolite.desc: A mysterious evolutionary lump. When held by a Pokémon that can still evolve, it raises both Defense and Sp. Def.

air-balloon.name: Air Balloon
air-balloon.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. The holder will float in the air until hit. Once the holder is hit, this item will burst.

white-herb.name: White Herb
white-herb.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It will restore any lowered stat in battle. It can be used only once.

power-herb.name: Power Herb
power-herb.desc: A single-use item to be held by a Pokémon. It allows the holder to immediately use a move that normally requires a turn to charge.

quick-powder.name: Quick Powder
quick-powder.desc: An item to be held by Ditto. Extremely fine yet hard, this odd powder boosts the Speed stat.

soothe-bell.name: Soothe Bell
soothe-bell.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. The comforting chime of this bell calms the holder, making it friendly.

smoke-ball.name: Smoke Ball
smoke-ball.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It enables the holder to flee from any wild Pokémon encounter without fail.

macho-brace.name: Macho Brace
macho-brace.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. This stiff, heavy brace helps Pokémon grow strong but cuts Speed in battle.

exp-share.name: Exp. Share
exp-share.desc: Turning on this special device will allow all the Pokémon on your team to receive Exp. Points from battles.

fire-stone.name: Fire Stone
fire-stone.desc: A peculiar stone that can make certain species of Pokémon evolve. The stone has a fiery orange heart.

water-stone.name: Water Stone
water-stone.desc: A peculiar stone that can make certain species of Pokémon evolve. It is the blue of a pool of clear water.

thunder-stone.name: Thunder Stone
thunder-stone.desc: A peculiar stone that can make certain species of Pokémon evolve. It has a distinct thunderbolt pattern.

leaf-stone.name: Leaf Stone
leaf-stone.desc: A peculiar stone that can make certain species of Pokémon evolve. It has an unmistakable leaf pattern.

moon-stone.name: Moon Stone
moon-stone.desc: A peculiar stone that can make certain species of Pokémon evolve. It is as black as the night sky.

sun-stone.name: Sun Stone
sun-stone.desc: A peculiar stone that can make certain species of Pokémon evolve. It burns as red as the evening sun.

shiny-stone.name: Shiny Stone
shiny-stone.desc: A peculiar stone that can make certain species of Pokémon evolve. It shines with a dazzling light.

dusk-stone.name: Dusk Stone
dusk-stone.desc: A peculiar stone that can make certain species of Pokémon evolve. It holds shadows as dark as can be.

dawn-stone.name: Dawn Stone
dawn-stone.desc: A peculiar stone that can make certain species of Pokémon evolve. It sparkles like a glittering eye.

ice-stone.name: Ice Stone
ice-stone.desc: A peculiar stone that can make certain species of Pokémon evolve. It has an unmistakable snowflake pattern.

rare-candy.name: Rare Candy
rare-candy.desc: A candy that is packed with energy. When consumed, it will instantly raise the level of a single Pokémon by one.

protein.name: Protein
protein.desc: A nutritious drink for Pokémon. When consumed, it raises the Attack base points of a single Pokémon.

iron.name: Iron
iron.desc: A nutritious drink for Pokémon. When consumed, it raises the Defense base points of a single Pokémon.

calcium.name: Calcium
calcium.desc: A nutritious drink for Pokémon. When consumed, it raises the Sp. Atk base points of a single Pokémon.

zinc.name: Zinc
zinc.desc: A nutritious drink for Pokémon. When consumed, it raises the Sp. Def base points of a single Pokémon.

carbos.name: Carbos
carbos.desc: A nutritious drink for Pokémon. When consumed, it raises the Speed base points of a single Pokémon.

hp-up.name: HP Up
hp-up.desc: A nutritious drink for Pokémon. When consumed, it raises the HP base points of a single Pokémon.

pp-up.name: PP Up
pp-up.desc: A medicine that slightly raises the max PP of a single selected move that has been learned by a Pokémon.

pp-max.name: PP Max
pp-max.desc: A medicine that optimally raises the max PP of a single selected move that has been learned by a Pokémon.

poke-ball.name: Poké Ball
poke-ball.desc: A device for catching wild Pokémon. It’s thrown like a ball at a Pokémon, comfortably encapsulating its target.

great-ball.name: Great Ball
great-ball.desc: A good, high-performance Poké Ball that provides a higher success rate for catching Pokémon than a standard Poké Ball.

ultra-ball.name: Ultra Ball
ultra-ball.desc: An ultra-high-performance Poké Ball that provides a higher success rate for catching Pokémon than a Great Ball.

master-ball.name: Master Ball
master-ball.desc: The best Poké Ball with the ultimate level of performance. With it, you will catch any wild Pokémon without fail.

potion.name: Potion
potion.desc: A spray-type medicine for treating wounds. It can be used to restore 20 HP to a single Pokémon.

super-potion.name: Super Potion
super-potion.desc: A spray-type medicine for treating wounds. It can be used to restore 60 HP to a single Pokémon.

max-potion.name: Max Potion
max-potion.desc: A spray-type medicine for treating wounds. It can be used to completely restore the max HP of a single Pokémon.

revive.name: Revive
revive.desc: A medicine that can be used to revive a single Pokémon that has fainted. It also restores half of the Pokémon’s max HP.

max-revive.name: Max Revive
max-revive.desc: A medicine that can be used to revive a single Pokémon that has fainted. It also fully restores the Pokémon’s max HP.

repel.name: Repel
repel.desc: An item that prevents any low-level wild Pokémon from jumping out at you for a while.

escape-rope.name: Escape Rope
escape-rope.desc: A long and durable rope. Use it to escape instantly from locations like caves or dungeons. It can be used any number of times.

nugget.name: Nugget
nugget.desc: A nugget of the purest gold that gives off a lustrous gleam in direct light. It can be sold at a high price to shops.

star-piece.name: Star Piece
star-piece.desc: A small shard of a beautiful gem that gives off a distinctly red sparkle. It can be sold at a high price to shops.

stardust.name: Stardust
stardust.desc: Lovely red sand that flows between the fingers with a loose, silky feel. It can be sold at a low price to shops.

comet-shard.name: Comet Shard
comet-shard.desc: A shard that fell to the ground when a comet approached. It can be sold at a high price to shops.

x-attack.name: X Attack
x-attack.desc: An item that sharply boosts the Attack stat of a Pokémon during a battle. It wears off once the Pokémon is withdrawn.

x-defense.name: X Defense
x-defense.desc: An item that sharply boosts the Defense stat of a Pokémon during a battle. It wears off once the Pokémon is withdrawn.

x-speed.name: X Speed
x-speed.desc: An item that sharply boosts the Speed stat of a Pokémon during a battle. It wears off once the Pokémon is withdrawn.

dire-hit.name: Dire Hit
dire-hit.desc: An item that greatly raises the critical-hit ratio of a Pokémon during a battle. It can be used only once and wears off if the Pokémon is withdrawn.

ether.name: Ether
ether.desc: This medicine can be used to restore 10 PP to a single selected move that has been learned by a Pokémon.

elixir.name: Elixir
elixir.desc: This medicine can be used to restore 10 PP to each of the moves that have been learned by a Pokémon.

max-elixir.name: Max Elixir
max-elixir.desc: This medicine can be used to fully restore the PP of all of the moves that have been learned by a Pokémon.

honey.name: Honey
honey.desc: A sweet honey collected by Pokémon. It has a lush aroma and can be sold at a low price to shops.

cleanse-tag.name: Cleanse Tag
cleanse-tag.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It helps keep wild Pokémon away if the holder is the head of the party.

everstone.name: Everstone
everstone.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. A Pokémon holding this peculiar stone is prevented from evolving.

lucky-punch.name: Lucky Punch
lucky-punch.desc: An item to be held by Chansey. This pair of lucky boxing gloves will boost Chansey’s critical-hit ratio.

big-nugget.name: Big Nugget
big-nugget.desc: A big nugget of pure gold that gives off a lustrous gleam. It can be sold at a high price to shops.

grip-claw.name: Grip Claw
grip-claw.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It extends the duration of multi-turn attacks, such as Bind and Wrap.

berry-juice.name: Berry Juice
berry-juice.desc: A 100 percent pure juice made of Berries. It can be used to restore 20 HP to a single Pokémon.

flame-orb.name: Flame Orb
flame-orb.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It’s a bizarre orb that will afflict the holder with a burn during battle.

toxic-orb.name: Toxic Orb
toxic-orb.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It’s a bizarre orb that will badly poison the holder during battle.

snowball.name: Snowball
snowball.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It boosts Attack if the holder is hit with an Ice-type attack. It can only be used once.

binding-band.name: Binding Band
binding-band.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It’s a band that increases the power of binding moves used by the holder.

adrenaline-orb.name: Adrenaline Orb
adrenaline-orb.desc: If held by a Pokémon, it boosts Speed when intimidated.

stick.name: Leek
stick.desc: An item to be held by Farfetch’d. This very long and stiff stalk of leek boosts its critical-hit ratio.

razor-fang.name: Razor Fang
razor-fang.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. When the holder successfully inflicts damage, the target may also flinch.

cell-battery.name: Cell Battery
cell-battery.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It boosts Attack if the holder is hit with an Electric-type attack. It can only be used once.

reaper-cloth.name: Reaper Cloth
reaper-cloth.desc: A cloth imbued with horrifyingly strong spiritual energy. It’s loved by a certain Pokémon.

electirizer.name: Electirizer
electirizer.desc: A box packed with a tremendous amount of electric energy. It’s loved by a certain Pokémon.

adamant-orb.name: Adamant Orb
adamant-orb.desc: A brightly gleaming orb to be held by Dialga. It boosts the power of Dragon- and Steel-type moves when it is held.

smooth-rock.name: Smooth Rock
smooth-rock.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It extends the duration of the move Sandstorm when used by the holder.

white-flute.name: White Flute
white-flute.desc: A flute made from white glass. It makes it easier to encounter weak Pokémon in the place you use it.

shed-shell.name: Shed Shell
shed-shell.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. This discarded carapace enables the holder to switch out of battle without fail.

protector.name: Protector
protector.desc: A protective item of some sort. It is extremely stiff and heavy. It’s loved by a certain Pokémon.

griseous-orb.name: Griseous Orb
griseous-orb.desc: A glowing orb to be held by Giratina. It boosts the power of Dragon- and Ghost-type moves when it is held.

lustrous-orb.name: Lustrous Orb
lustrous-orb.desc: A beautifully glowing orb to be held by Palkia. It boosts the power of Dragon- and Water-type moves when it is held.

soul-dew.name: Soul Dew
soul-dew.desc: A wondrous orb to be held by either Latios or Latias. It raises the power of Psychic- and Dragon-type moves.

silver-wing.name: Silver Wing
silver-wing.desc: A strange, silvery feather that sparkles.

rainbow-wing.name: Rainbow Wing
rainbow-wing.desc: A mystical rainbow feather that sparkles.

bicycle.name: Bicycle
bicycle.desc: A folding Bicycle that enables a rider to get around much faster than a pair of Running Shoes will allow.

soda-pop.name: Soda Pop
soda-pop.desc: A highly carbonated soda drink. It can be used to restore 50 HP to a single Pokémon.

iron-ball.name: Iron Ball
iron-ball.desc: An item to be held by a Pokémon. It lowers Speed and allows Ground-type moves to hit Flying types and holders that are levitating.

thick-club.name: Thick Club
thick-club.desc: An item to be held by Cubone or Marowak. It’s a hard bone of some sort that boosts the Attack stat.

metal-powder.name: Metal Powder
metal-powder.desc: An item to be held by Ditto. Extremely fine yet hard, this odd powder boosts the Defense stat.

rage-candy-bar.name: Rage Candy Bar
rage-candy-bar.desc: Mahogany Town’s famous candy. It can be used once to heal all the status conditions of a Pokémon.

fresh-water.name: Fresh Water
fresh-water.desc: Water with high mineral content. It can be used to restore 30 HP to a single Pokémon.

full-heal.name: Full Heal
full-heal.desc: A spray-type medicine that is broadly effective. It can be used to heal all the status conditions of a single Pokémon.

burn-heal.name: Burn Heal
burn-heal.desc: A spray-type medicine for treating burns. It can be used to heal a single Pokémon suffering from a burn.

ice-heal.name: Ice Heal
ice-heal.desc: A spray-type medicine for treating freezing. It can be used to thaw out a single Pokémon that has been frozen solid.

paralyze-heal.name: Paralyze Heal
paralyze-heal.desc: A spray-type medicine for treating paralysis. It can be used to free a single Pokémon that has been paralyzed.

awakening.name: Awakening
awakening.desc: A spray-type medicine to wake the sleeping. It can be used to rouse a single Pokémon from the clutches of sleep.

antidote.name: Antidote
antidote.desc: A spray-type medicine for treating poisoning. It can be used to lift the effects of being poisoned from a single Pokémon.

poke-flute.name: Poké Flute
poke-flute.desc: A flute that can play with such a beautiful tone that even sleeping Pokémon find themselves woken up.

coin-case.name: Coin Case
coin-case.desc: A case for holding coins obtained at the Game Corner. It can hold up to 50,000 coins.

old-rod.name: Old Rod
old-rod.desc: An old and beat-up fishing rod. Use it at any body of water to fish for wild aquatic Pokémon.

silph-scope.name: Silph Scope
silph-scope.desc: A scope that lets you see what cannot usually be seen. It is made by Silph Co.

guard-spec.name: Guard Spec.
guard-spec.desc: An item that prevents stat reduction among the Trainer’s party Pokémon for five turns after it is used in battle.

lemonade.name: Lemonade
lemonade.desc: A very sweet and refreshing drink. It can be used to restore 70 HP to a single Pokémon.

poke-doll.name: Poké Doll
poke-doll.desc: A doll that attracts the attention of a Pokémon. It guarantees escape from any battle with wild Pokémon.

ss-ticket.name: S.S. Ticket
ss-ticket.desc: A ticket required for sailing on the ferry S.S. Aqua. It has a drawing of a ship on its front.

max-ether.name: Max Ether
max-ether.desc: This medicine can be used to fully restore the PP of a single selected move that has been learned by a Pokémon.

secret-key.name: Secret Key
secret-key.desc: A high-tech key that has to be used at a specific location. It emits a special electronic signal to open a door.

dowsing-machine.name: Dowsing Machine
dowsing-machine.desc: A high-tech machine that shows the location of invisible items. It’s attached to the head when in use.

gold-teeth.name: Gold Teeth
gold-teeth.desc: A set of golden false teeth lost by the Safari Zone’s warden. They make his smile sparkle.
